newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-PORTUGAL WIN KEEPS WORLD CUP HOPES ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PORTUGAL WIN KEEPS WORLD CUP HOPES ALIVE.

text.p: Portugal boosted their chances of reaching the World Cup finals with a spirited 1-0 victory over Ukraine in an European group qualifying match on Saturday.

Although the talented Portuguese failed to turn their near total dominance of the game into a string of goals, it was a fine performance against a determined Ukrainian side that had clearly come to defend after their 2-1 home win a month ago.

Portugal, desperately needing a win after a disappointing start to their campaign to qualify for the 1998 finals in France, finally got the goal they deserved after 58 minutes when Fernando Couto drove home from close range.
But it needed a defensive error by the resolute Ukrainians to break the deadlock.
Yuri Maksimov's diving header after a Portuguese free-kick on the left of the box only turned the ball into the path of the Barcelona defender who fired it into the roof of the net.
After going one down, the Ukrainians pushed forward but they lacked the pace to worry the solid Portuguese defence on a pitch made slippery by the heavy humidity.
"It was difficult but we played with great patience," said a relieved Portuguese coach Artur Jorge. "We could have scored a couple but they defended tightly."
The win takes the Portuguese to the top of their qualifying group from which only one side wins automatic passage to the finals.
Portugal has seven points from four games, one more than Ukraine and three more than Germany. But they have also played more games than their principal rivals.
"We did not have much luck but the Portuguese played very well," said Ukrainian coach Josef Szabo. But he added that Germany's 1-1 draw at home to Northern Ireland left the group wide open.
The Portuguese attacked from the start and could have gone ahead after 20 minutes but goalkeeper Oleh Suslov dived quickly to his right to block Luis Figo's volley.
Joao Vieira Pinto should have done better when a cross from the left by defender Dimas Teixeira found him unmarked in front of goal but he could only manage a weak header.
For most of the first half, Ukrainian striker Serhiy Rebrov was a lone figure in the Portuguese half as his team mates opted to defend in their own territory.
Szabo sent on Hennady Zubov in place of Serhiy Yesin at the start of the second half to strength the attack down the right flank but the visitors had few clear chances to score.
The nearest they came was when a shot by Yuri Maksimov took a deflection and nearly lobbed over the head of Baia with just minutes remaining.
Earlier, Joao Vieira Pinto almost gave the Portuguese a second goal when he turned brilliantly in the area but his well-struck shot flew past the post.

Portugal 1-Vitor Baia, 2-Joao Pinto, 3-Dimas Teixeira, 4-Oceano Cruz, 5-Fernando Couto, 6-Helder Cristovao, 7-Luis Figo, 8-Joao Vieira Pinto, 9-Ricardo Sa Pinto (Paulo Bento 76), 10-Rui Costa (Sergio Conceicao 65), 11-Antonio Folha (Hugo Porfirio 45).

Ukraine 1-Oleh Suslov, 2-Yuri Dmytrulin, 3-Viktor Skrypnyk, 4-Olexander Holovko, 5-Serhiy Bezhenar, 6-Serhiy Popov, 7-Yuri Maksimov, 8-Yuri Kalitvintsev (Valery Kryventsov 58), 9-Hennady Orbu (Vitaly Kosovsky 65), 10-Serhiy Yesin (Hennady Zubov 45), 11-Serhiy Rebrov.
